source: Austria and German state portals sweep (Landesarchiv NRW sufservice API, Saxon State Archives), 9 Nov 2026
title: B. G. Niebuhr, Amsterdam, to Freiherr vom Stein: letter largely in a four-digit numeric code
correspondents: Barthold Georg Niebuhr (Prussian loan negotiator, Amsterdam) -> Karl vom und zum Stein
shelfmark: Landesarchiv NRW / Vereinigte Westfälische Adelsarchive, Nachlass Freiherr vom Stein, Cap.C.I - S 1199,11
folio_note: 14 images; leaf 001 viewed: two lines of German ('Euer Excellenz, konnte ich noch mit letzter Post den richtigen Empfang der von Herrn Bandirector Hundt ... Documente melden') then about 17 lines of numerals from 300 to 3100
status: 9 Nov 2026 (Brice Dudout, issue #359, not checked by the project): page 1 transcribed (265 groups, all at or below 3123); the cribs S 1230,04 (Wilhelm) and S 1116,1 (Goltz) use other repertories; the printed editions (Hubatsch's Stein edition, Niebuhr's letters) were not checked. Earlier: Archive record: 'egh.; chiffriert', digitised (DFG-Viewer). Viewed leaf 001: number groups after the opening lines, no plaintext between them. Other Stein letters of 1808 in the Nachlass are catalogued 'dechiffriert' (Goltz, Humboldt) or carry plaintext between the lines (Prince Wilhelm of Prussia, Paris, 24 Jan 1808, S 1230,04, also a four-digit code), which gives cribs and a probable key family.
why: Dated, digitised, named writer and recipient in the Prussian reform crisis (Niebuhr's Amsterdam loan; Stein dismissed two weeks later); the interlined S 1230,04 letter in the same kind of code should supply cribs.
score_note: Scored 9 Nov 2026 after viewing leaves 001 and 002 of S 1199,11 and leaf 001 of S 1230,04
verify: Check the Stein edition (Briefe und amtliche Schriften, vol. 10, Briefwechsel 1808, De Gruyter 2015, section 'November 1808') for a printed decipherment before promoting.
access_note: free scans on lwl.org (Lesesaal-Digitalisate/C_Adelsarchive/Cap/Cap.C.I/Cap.C.I_S 1199,11/)
prior_art: not settled (9 Nov 2026): known.py finds nothing on 'Niebuhr', 'Cap.C.I' or 1199,11; one web search found no edition text; the modern Stein edition (2015) probably prints the letter and may give the decipherment, not checked. DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry not searched.
vetting_note: Leaf 001 and 003 of Cap.C.I S 1199,11 viewed: German salutation + two lines, then about 16-19 lines of 3-4 digit dot-separated groups (300-3100, many with dash/tick marks), no plaintext between, no decipherment on the leaves; verso 002 blank with 'Steinsches Archiv' stamp. But the printed-edition check could not be done: Botzenhart 'Briefwechsel' II (1931), Stein 'Briefe und amtliche Schriften' / 2015 De Gruyter 'Briefwechsel' (section Nov 1808), Pertz and Niebuhr 'Lebensnachrichten' are not online/readable here (web searches x4 found no text, DECODE/Tomokiyo/Lasry no hit). A printed decipherment is plausible, so not promotable until a volume is checked.
